content.overview: Flame-resistant clothing chars instead of melting, buying seconds of escape time in flash fire. It does not make the wearer fireproof; it limits burn injury when every second counts. Standard grade: baseline NFPA-rated flame resistance in real materials.
details: Heat flux is measured in kW/m2 or cal/cm2-s; a flash fire delivers about 84 kW/m2 (2 cal/cm2-s).
Time to second-degree burn is roughly TPP divided by heat flux: a TPP-12 fabric at 2 cal/cm2-s gives about 6 seconds.
Charring fibers form an insulating carbon layer that slows heat transfer; melting fibers stick to skin and worsen burns.
Limiting oxygen index above 21 means the fiber self-extinguishes in normal air; higher LOI means harder to keep burning.
specifications: Nomex (meta-aramid): chars at about 427 C, never melts or drips; limiting oxygen index near 28-30.
